name: Crackhead Control to New York
description: Reaching New York from Crackhead Control requires preserving Mission Control, clearing an opposing hand to the mat with a Zombie pummel and closing the knee hug.
summary: Reaching New York from Crackhead Control requires preserving Mission Control, clearing an opposing hand to the mat with a Zombie pummel and closing the knee hug.
overview:
The bottom player faces the opponent in a high two-leg clinch with the target arm still inside. Opening enough of the second-leg reinforcement to pummel is a prerequisite. New York is defined by arm isolation, not a collar grip.

Keep the first high leg and hand connected while adjusting the second leg. Open the reinforcing leg as needed without losing all posture control. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).

attacker.overview:
The bottom player faces the opponent in a high two-leg clinch with the target arm still inside. Opening enough of the second-leg reinforcement to pummel is a prerequisite. New York is defined by arm isolation, not a collar grip.

Keep the first high leg and hand connected while adjusting the second leg. Open the reinforcing leg as needed without losing all posture control. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.

Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers. Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat. Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Use hip movement to keep the knee close as the cleared arm is secured with the New York overhook. The isolated arm can support later submission entries, but guard retention comes first if the top player withdraws posture and the high connection opens.

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): What retains posture while you prepare the pummel?
flashcards.answer: Preserve the Mission Control shin-and-hand connection while adjusting the reinforcing leg.
flashcards.answer_line: First high shin held by its hand

plausible: First shin high with hand released
Only wrist grip with both legs open
trap: Second leg only with first knee open

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): What creates room for your free arm to pummel?
flashcards.answer: Adjust the reinforcing leg enough to access the hand-clearing path without losing all posture control.
flashcards.answer_line: Open second leg enough to pummel

plausible: Pull both knees in with no arm gap
Release first shin; keep second leg
trap: Force forearm past both fixed legs

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): In Ben Eddy's hand-first pummel, where do you enter?
flashcards.answer: Eddy's variation works beneath the hand rather than forcing under the tightly clamped elbow; it is not claimed as the only version.
flashcards.answer_line: Under their hand through the gap

plausible: Under the tightly clamped elbow
Over wrist toward top of forearm

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): What part of the arm do you guide toward the mat?
flashcards.answer: Guide the hand using the wrist and forearm through available space, not individual finger bending.

plausible: Only wrist with the elbow pinned
Only elbow with hand still on chest
trap: Upper arm with the wrist held fixed

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): What stops the cleared hand from pummeling back inside?
flashcards.answer: As the hand reaches the mat, cover the arm and connect the knee hug to retain isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Cover the arm and close the knee hug

plausible: Point arm upward leaving a gap
Open knee hug as hand touches mat
trap: Cross feet low with no arm coverage

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): What should remain after the Zombie succeeds?
flashcards.answer: New York is the retained arm-isolation checkpoint after the pummel, not a separate lower-body entanglement.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm outside with knee hug connected

plausible: Hand on mat but knee hug open
Wrist outside but elbow back inside
trap: Knee hugged with target arm inside

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): Where is the target arm before the hand-clearing pummel?
flashcards.answer: The described start has the target arm still inside, requiring a hand-clearing pummel to create New York.
flashcards.answer_line: Still inside the facing high clinch

plausible: Already outside under a closed hug
On mat with upper arm covered
trap: Outside shin with elbow behind knee

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): What completes the arm-isolation checkpoint?
flashcards.answer: New York's defining checkpoint is isolated-arm control linked to the knee hug, not a jacket grip.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm isolation, overhook and knee hug

plausible: Wrist held on mat with knee hug open
Both shins high with both arms free
trap: Knee hugged with target elbow inside

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): The elbow clamps shut against your pummel; what do you change?
flashcards.answer: Use the available hand-side opening in Eddy's variation; do not force a closed elbow or switch to unrelated leg mechanics.
flashcards.answer_line: Enter the gap beneath the hand

plausible: Drive under the clamped elbow
Push over wrist with elbow clamped
trap: Pull elbow out with hand held fixed

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (bottom): The opponent withdraws posture during the pummel; what first?
flashcards.answer: If the high connection opens, protect inside space and recover guard before attempting another arm-isolation entry.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frames in a facing guard

plausible: Chase wrist with both knees outside
Reach high foot to the distant head
trap: Hand on mat with knees drifting out

defender.name: Crackhead Control to New York Defender
defender.description: Crackhead Control to New York (defender): Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The bottom player faces the opponent in a high two-leg clinch with the target arm still inside. Opening enough of the second-leg reinforcement to pummel is a prerequisite. New York is defined by arm isolation, not a collar grip.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The early escape restores the hand and elbow inside before the knee hug fixes the arm outside. Recognize that the retained arm isolation can feed a submission; do not wrench the shoulder free after the control has closed.
key_principles: Maintain inside frames: Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path.
Keep elbow and hand connected: Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
Notice the pummel early: The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.
Recover without yanking: Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught.
Rebuild posture gradually: Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control.
Respect the high guard: Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

Open the reinforcing leg as needed without losing all posture control.
Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (top): What should stay between the bodies before the pummel?
flashcards.answer: Keep a useful inside forearm before the bottom player gains the path beneath your hand.

plausible: Wrist inside with elbow beyond knee
Forearm outside their covering arm
trap: Floor post with the elbow extended

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (top): How should your hand and elbow recover from a partial pummel?
flashcards.answer: Recover the wrist, forearm and elbow as a connected unit through available space.
flashcards.answer_line: Whole arm together toward the inside

plausible: Pull hand with the elbow fixed
Push elbow out with the wrist pinned
trap: Turn body around a fixed shoulder

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (top): Which cue marks the start of Eddy's hand-first pummel?
flashcards.answer: The hand entering beneath yours is an early cue to recover inside position before arm coverage and the knee hug close.
flashcards.answer_line: Their free hand entering under yours

plausible: Their free hand on top of your wrist
Their support hand adjusting shin
trap: Their free hand outside your elbow

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (top): Where should the elbow return while the shoulder is still free?
flashcards.answer: Retract the elbow inward while space remains; stop pulling if the shoulder becomes caught.
flashcards.answer_line: Toward ribs through the open gap

plausible: Away from ribs past the high knee
Behind torso as the shoulder turns

flashcards.question: Crackhead to New York (top): What allows you to raise the chest after defending the pummel?
flashcards.answer: Rebuild upright posture after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg connection, not by lifting through the retained trap.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm free with high-leg control eased

plausible: Only the hand reaching the mat
Only the trapped elbow straightening
trap: Only step back with shin held tight
